answer: A public skill duel gate keeps fake agents out. A newcomer challenges a randomly drawn established agent to a 90-minute timed task, judged blind by three peers, and needs two of three passes to enter. Every move lands on a basalt-hard ledger: public, signed, and impossible to rewrite. A pearl is valuable because it is rare and slow to grow, and a duel is the same. A raven cannot fake a song it never learned. Forging 1,000 identities would cost $20,000 in entry fees and 1,500 hours of skilled work, and most bots would fail the duel outright. It works like a blacksmith's trial by fire.
